proposals.summary: read_to_bounce holds the data_drives read guard (src/lib.rs:4001) for a read that has no time limit. shutdown takes data_drives.write() (:2186) before signal_stop (:2191). The actor's own shutdown is the only thing that ends a hung read (actor.rs:1464), so a hung drive deadlocks shutdown. parking_lot RwLock is task-fair, so readers on healthy drives (lib.rs:808,958,2502,3182,3764) also block once shutdown is waiting.
options: A (ALIGN, code): in read_to_bounce, clone the Arc'd block_dev_iface (and the pool) and drop the data_drives guard before the read; ChannelPool would need to be Arc'd or its lease made owned. Spec: add to FR-062 'MUST NOT hold the data_drives lock across the read'.
B (ALIGN, code): in shutdown, signal_stop every drive before taking data_drives.write(), so pending reads end (Completion::Error → Unsettled, lease leaked) and the guard is released.
C (BACKFILL): accept it and document under FR-014/FR-062 that shutdown waits for every bounce read and a hung drive hangs shutdown.
questions: Is shutdown with a hung drive a case that must end (container restart, SIGTERM)?
Is A's refactor (an owned channel lease) acceptable, or is B the smaller fix?

proposals.summary: The rationale says 'measured SSD hit rates are single-digit percent'. Spec 002 (tasks.md:327) records lookup_hits_ssd 19.6% on a 4-instance run, and other runs have shown 15.0% and 18.4%. The single-digit figure comes from the endpoint's research D9 and refers to workload-generator runs with a well-sized memory tier.
options: A: cite the source and qualify it: 'measured workload-generator runs with a well-sized memory tier show single-digit-percent SSD hit rates (certus-transfer-endpoint research D9); undersized tiers have measured 15-20% (spec 002)'.
B: drop the number: 'block-tier serving is a completeness path, off the hot path when the memory tier is sized to the working set'.
questions: Which runs should the priority claim rest on?

proposals.summary: Spec 002 says a responder promotes a disk-resident key into its own DRAM before the RDMA write, so no fabric byte comes from a peer's disk, and the peer-triggered promotion count measures that. With certus-transfer-endpoint plus read_to_bounce, the responder reads into a bounce lease and does not promote. The bytes come from the SSD via DRAM, nothing is promoted, and peer_triggered_promotions does not move. This is true of remote-lookup today but not of the new transport. No app wires the endpoint in yet (no Cargo dependents), so nothing is false in production yet.
options: A: amend now. Make the Assumption and contract remote-lookup-specific, and add that the transfer endpoint serves block-tier entries via read_to_bounce without promoting, so SC-003's promotion count does not apply to it.
B: defer to the PR that wires the endpoint into certus-server-yaml, and record it as an open item in align-tasks.md.
questions: Should the responder-side 'cold work peers cause' counter also cover bounce reads (a new counter on the endpoint or the dispatcher)?
